messages:
maria: Heads-up: APAC -> SFO netlink degradation observed starting ~2026-03-18 17:08 UTC. We're seeing ~30-40% packet loss on the primary p2p links; several Dedicated zones report high GPU queue times. Kicking off incident.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created · priority=P1 · affected_region=apac · impact=degraded_throughput+high_latency
kevin: Copy. Are we on automatic region failover? Which routing policy triggered?
alex: apac->sfo traffic-shift started automatically via policy `route:latency_based_v2`. We shifted ~40% initially but sfo hit headroom limits quickly -> token throttles / queuing. Posting metrics snapshot in #eng-telemetry.
maria: Confirmed we failed over shards A1/A2. Warm pools didn't spin up fast enough; observed warm_pool_spinup p95 ~ 18s (target 6s). KPIs: token latency +220ms p50->p50, ~18% requests retried upstream. Ops is scaling burst capacity now.
jess: I've initiated a temporary placement increase: sfo-burst +10 GPUs, rebalancer is moving load. ETA for full capacity on those nodes ~8m :hourglass:
kevin: Heads-up on cost — that burst eats into reserved budget. If sustained >$5k/hr we need finance sign-off. Who can approve emergency spend?
tara: I'll ping finance ops. For now keep burst at +4 GPUs unless queueing still severe.
alex: Note: we observed a cascade — when sfo reached headroom some requests retried back to apac, which kept oscillating. Need hysteresis in traffic shift logic.
alex: Metrics snippet:
```yaml
failover:
  thresholds:
    packet_loss_pct: 5    # current
    shift_pct_on_alert: 20
    shift_pct_on_escalation: 50
  warm_pool_min: 8
```
maria: Proposal (short):
- lower packet_loss_pct threshold to 3% for APAC routing
- increase warm_pool_min for apac pools to 12
- introduce a prebake/prewarm policy for critical model families (gptx-4x)
- add 30s hysteresis window before reversing traffic
I'll open a PR with playbook edits and a test plan.
sre-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/987 · branch=apac-failover-refactor
kevin: Also add an automated rolling-canary after shift: run a 30s synthetic workload that validates p99 latency, kv-cache fill < 80%, and token-success-rate > 99.5% before directing >50% traffic.
jess: Good call. I'll add that check to the router healthcheck and expose it on the console.
maria: Action items (owner -> ETA):
- PR review + merge -> alex/jess -> 24h
- Add synthetic p99 canary -> tara -> 48h
- Finance emergency budget approval -> tara/kevin -> ASAP
- Postmortem doc & runbook update -> maria -> 48h
- Dashboard + histogram for warm-pool spinup latency -> alex -> 72h
alex: I'll also add an emergency fallback: if target region headroom < 10% and p99 latency > threshold, route to quantized-model variant to preserve throughput. PR to ops-runtime incoming.
tara: Scheduling a runbook practice drill next week focused on traffic-shift and warm-pool scaling. Will include on-call rotation and run the canary flow.
maria: Retrospective notes to capture in postmortem: poor visibility into reserved capacity headroom, warm-pool spinup latency hard to correlate with prewarm config, and cost controls for emergency bursts need clearer guardrails.
sre-bot: INC-2026-042 status updated: mitigated at 19:33 UTC · mitigation_summary=traffic-shift + sfo-burst applied + prebake kicks in
maria: Thanks all — I'll post the formal postmortem doc and link the runbook PR when ready. Please add any missed actions to the thread.
kevin: Agree. After postmortem let's schedule a 30-minute sync with finance to define emergency burst thresholds and approval flow. :calendar:
jess: Closing ops note: rebalancer succeeded, tail latency back to normal in 22m. Will monitor for 24h and then mark incident resolved.
